newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-FREE-SPENDING ATLETICO SAY JUNINHO TRANSFER COMPLETED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FREE-SPENDING ATLETICO SAY JUNINHO TRANSFER COMPLETED.

text.p: Atletico Madrid have beaten off the challenge of Tottenham to sign Middlesbrough's Brazilian midfielder Juninho, club executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin claimed on Wednesday.
"Today we have confirmed 100 per cent the deal," said Gil Marin, son of club owner Jesus Gil, in an interview with the TVE1 television station.
"Juninho told the president of Tottenham...'thanks for your interest but the decision is already taken'."
Recent Spanish media reports have suggested Atletico would pay $20 million for Juninho compared with English premier league Tottenham's bid of $18.3 million.
Middlesbrough, who were relegated from the premier league last season, said on Tuesday they had accepted Tottenham's bid but that Juninho "certainly hadn't signed" for the north London club.
Juninho has repeatedly said he preferred a move to Spain.

In a hectic round of transfers in Spain on Wednesday, Atletico signed Christian Vieri from Juventus for $20 million and look set to pay another multi-million dollar fee for a fellow striker, Espanyol's Jordi Lardin.
Juventus general manager Luciano Moggi said Vieri had signed a four-year contract with the Spanish side.
Lardin is expected to undergo a medical in Madrid on Thursday and sign shortly afterwards.

Espanyol have already acquired Juan Eduardo Esnaider in exchange for Lardin and are likely to receive around 1.5 billion pesetas ($10.3 million) as well as a further player -- possibly midfielder Roberto Fresnedoso.
Argentine international Esnaider was presented as a new Espanyol player on Wednesday.
He had struggled to find his scoring touch in spells with both Atletico and Real Madrid after helping Zaragoza to the Cup Winners' Cup in 1995.
